title: Rate-limit password reset requests
user: A user who asks for more than five password resets in an hour sees a wait message instead of another email.

behaviors.before: Any number of reset emails per hour
behaviors.after: The sixth request in an hour is refused
behaviors.test: test/auth/reset-limiter.test.ts: refuses the sixth request, allows the first after the window
behaviors.detail: The limiter counts requests per lowercased email in the cache, and each count expires with the window. The controller checks it before queueing the email, so a refused request sends nothing. A counter older than the window never blocks a request.

behaviors.after: The form shows how long to wait
behaviors.test: test/web/reset-form.test.tsx: renders the wait message from retry-after
behaviors.detail: The controller returns 429 with a retry-after header and the form reads it into the message. Any other error keeps the existing generic text.

behaviors.before: An unused legacy reset endpoint ships
behaviors.detail: The route was never registered after the router rewrite. The build proves nothing imports it.

flows.name: User requests a password reset
steps: Open the sign-in page and choose Forgot password
Submit the same email six times within an hour
The sixth submit shows the wait message and sends no email

flows.name: Operator reads the audit log
flows.effect: Each refused request logs the email hash and the retry time, so support can see why a user got no email.

changed_files: Counts reset requests per email and refuses at six
The count lives beside the token store so a restart does not clear it
Asks the limiter before queueing the email
The controller is the one place every reset request passes through
Leaving it is a second reset path with no limiter on it
Shows the wait message on a 429 response
A bare 429 reads as a broken form, so the wait has to be named

questions.detail: The cache already expires entries on its own and is shared across instances. The database adds a migration for a value that expires in an hour. In memory breaks with more than one instance.

questions.q: What does the sixth request return?
questions.detail: A 429 lets the form explain the wait. A silent 200 hides the limit from the user and from support.
